🤖 **Analysis — no PR (out of agent scope)**

This is an experiment / production hero-run launch, not a self-contained bug fix, so I am not opening a PR.

**Why:**
- The deliverable is a production-priority v4-2048 Iris submission of the 67B qk=1.75 262K context-extension run. Launching production training needs cluster resources and explicit human approval; AGENTS.md and the hero-run workflow keep this off the automated-fix path.
- The only code delta is a one-line skew bump. It belongs in the author's existing stack, not a parallel PR. [`long_context_datakit_moe_mix.py:15`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8791/files) currently reads `LONG_CONTEXT_SKEW = 4`; the 8x twin sets `LONG_CONTEXT_SKEW = 8`.
- That file and the launcher module are only on the open, stacked branches [#8656](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8656) (2x, adds the mix + launchers + test) → [#8791](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8791) (4x). Neither is merged, so an agent PR would duplicate in-flight work — the fix-issue duplicate-work preflight says hand off instead.

**Proposed approach for a human (author @Helw150):**
1. Land the stack (#8656, then #8791).
2. Stack an 8x branch that sets `LONG_CONTEXT_SKEW = 8`, resolving the run to `..._longctx_skew8` and a fresh output path, matching the planned W&B id `moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep1_ctx4_bs256_seq262144_ctxext_step156k_qk175_longctx_skew8`.
3. Extend `tests/test_june_67b_long_context_mixture.py` to assert the 8x component renormalizes to fixed outer domain-by-quality weights and the stated ~43.405% aggregate share of `>65,536`-token documents — this is the one meaningful, non-tautological check for the skew change.
4. Submit at production priority from the pinned launcher per the logbook command and verify startup from `step-156000`.

Steps 2–4 preserve the step-156000 checkpoint, 1000-step schedule, MuonH, batch size 256, `resume_data_offset=7,296,000`, and the `(1, 256, 4, 1, 1)` mesh. Leaving this to the author since it is a live production run on a stack they own.
